dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Couldn't be more at home! a true Knight of Boreas can build his den anywhere.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Animals adapt to their environment to survive. I've got personal experience in that regard — both after and during the expedition.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Some animals conceal themselves to avoid predators, often hiding in inhospitable terrain.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Thorny bushes, perilous cliffs... the spires of the Favonius Cathedral, the rooftop of a certain knightly headquarters...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Um, those last two don't seem quite right...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, those were my hiding spots after escaping the office! The others gradually got quite good at finding me, though.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: These days... I'd probably have to hide behind the wind barriers in Stormterror's Lair, or Dragonspine's peak during a blizzard...

choices.text: Maybe you could just stay here...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Thanks, but I'd rather do without. Sleeping more soundly would lower my alertness and ability to make a quick getaway.

choices.text: I can make you another pillow if you need one.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Yup. It took us through lots of desolate, dangerous terrain — we often had to make camp in hostile surroundings.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: We took cots and tents, of course, but there were some nights when we had no time to set them up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Didn't you have your own special tent?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I did, but when my troops were freezing, I could hardly sleep soundly in comfort, could I? I always let the wounded use my tent instead.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: *sigh* If only we had a teapot like this...

choices.text: You make yourself sound like a wild animal...
